rationale:
Issue #1799 documents a pre-existing spec violation (RFC 7540 §5.4.2): after the client sends RST_STREAM and drops the id from _openStreams, an in-flight server HeadersFrame for that id falls into the 'clients cannot receive HEADER_FRAMEs as a connection attempt' branch, which _catchProtocolErrors escalates into a forceful teardown of the whole connection, killing unrelated streams. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in pkgs/http2/lib/src/streams/stream_handler.dart that replaces the connection-level ProtocolException with the stream-scoped _throwStreamClosedException(frame.header.streamId), aligning header-frame handling with the pre-existing data-frame handling described in the commit message. No unrelated refactor, feature extension, or config/doc change is present: the CHANGELOG and pubspec bumps live in the sibling commit 0bed60a and are excluded from all three production patch variants; patches/trigger-tests.patch contains only the added clientTest and no edits to existing cases. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test 'header-frame-received-after-stream-cancel' and it exercises exactly the reported scenario: two open streams, terminate stream1, server writes a HeadersFrame for streamId1, then the test asserts stream2 still receives its DataFrame and client.isOpen is true. It uses only pre-existing public APIs (makeRequest, outgoingMessages.close, terminate, incomingMessages, finish, FrameWriter.writeHeadersFrame); _throwStreamClosedException is a private helper referenced only from production code, so the trigger does not depend on any new production API. Strict evidence confirms the differential without any inference on my part: trigger.buggy_differential reproduced test/client_test.dart::header-frame-received-after-stream-cancel, trigger.fixed_clean and full_suite.fixed_all_green passed, buggy full-suite failures were confined to the declared trigger, and determinism held over 3 repetitions across a complete 32-run matrix, both pre- and post-minimization with zero failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #1799 is not a duplicate of any active registry entry, and it matches the single allowed verified issue key.

Issue #1799 describes a precise pre-existing defect: after the client sends RST_STREAM and removes the stream from _openStreams, an in-flight server HeadersFrame for that id falls into the 'server cannot open new streams' branch of StreamHandler._processStreamFrameInternal, raising a connection-level ProtocolException that _catchProtocolErrors escalates to a forceful teardown of the whole connection, killing unrelated streams. This contradicts RFC 7540 §5.4.2, quoted in the issue. The minimized production patch is a single hunk in pkgs/http2/lib/src/streams/stream_handler.dart that replaces that connection-scoped ProtocolException with the stream-scoped _throwStreamClosedException(frame.header.streamId), aligning header-frame handling with the already-correct data-frame path; the only other lines touched are the explanatory comment inside the same hunk, so there is no unrelated refactor, formatting, feature, docs, config, or test change (CHANGELOG/pubspec live in the sibling commit 0bed60a and are excluded). The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fix commit, clientTest('header-frame-received-after-stream-cancel'), which reproduces the reported scenario end to end: two streams opened, stream1 terminated, server then writes a HeadersFrame for stream1's id, and the test asserts the connection stays open and stream2 still receives its DataFrame. It uses only pre-existing public API (makeRequest, terminate, incomingMessages, FrameWriter); _throwStreamClosedException is referenced but not defined by the patch, and the buggy revision built and ran the test to a differential failure, confirming no dependence on new production API. Strict machine evidence reports all gates green in both original and post-minimization runs: build.both_versions passed, trigger.buggy_differential reproduced test/client_test.dart::header-frame-received-after-stream-cancel, trigger.fixed_clean and full_suite.fixed_all_green passed, trigger.deterministic with 3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions and a 32-run matrix. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and dart-lang/http#1799 is the sole allowed key, so the root cause is not a duplicate.

risks: The test asserts an extra client-sent RstStreamFrame for streamId1 that its own comment calls non-required current behavior, so the trigger is partly coupled to implementation detail rather than the spec requirement alone.
